Apple iPhone prices: Surge in memory and component costs leads to major price hikes for some models

Increased pricing likely to persist for years, and may never come back down

9to5Mac readers have already been skeptical about whether Apple will reduce prices once the component shortage eases. More than two-thirds of readers indicated they expect this price increase to be permanent.

A subsequent analyst report noted that supply chain pricing will not improve at all until 2028; even when the market eases then, the effect will be quite limited. Based on the current situation, the extremely high pricing is very likely to remain for at least several years, and may never return to previous levels.

If that's the case, how will you respond? Will you grit your teeth and continue purchasing Apple products at the same pace? Will you reduce the quantity or frequency of Apple product purchases? Or will you take other measures, such as buying a cheaper model, choosing a refurbished unit, or waiting for a price drop before making a move?

Please take part in our poll and share your thoughts in the comments. The poll allows multiple selections, so you can have more than one plan to change your purchasing habits.
